summary: Clustered OAuth refresh-token rotations observed for multiple service accounts after external referrer click
description:
Issue summary: Security team flagged a burst of refresh-token exchange events and subsequent session creations for three internal service accounts following clicks on an externally-hosted recruiting form. Pattern: concentrated token rotations in <2 hour windows tied to the same HTTP Referrer value. Impact: potential unauthorized session creation and risk of lateral access; no confirmed data exfiltration at time of triage.

Context: On 2026-03-12 10:20 UTC a support alert from the auth-monitoring rule 'refresh-exchange-rate' triggered. Initial automated blocks prevented some exchanges but logs show multiple successful exchanges and new session tokens issued to internal service principals. The affected accounts are mostly service/service-account style identities used by integrations and vendor onboarding flows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Reproduce not attempted on prod; replicate flow in staging by following recruiting form redirect sequence used by vendor.
2) Simulate inbound OAuth refresh with an external referrer header and observe token-exchange logs.
3) Replay recorded refresh-token value in a hardened test environment to validate token acceptance behavior.
observed_logs: 2026-03-12T10:21:05Z auth-service POST /oauth/token grant_type=refresh_token svc-data-pipeline client_id=internal-client status=200 referrer=https://jobforms.vendor-example[.]com/redirect?u=...
Subtotal: 102 refresh exchanges for svc-data-pipeline between 10:20-11:45 UTC
New bearer tokens issued and active sessions created from 3 unique ASN-prefixed IP clusters (Atlanta, Warsaw, Lisbon)
comments: Support (Avery Chen) - 2026-03-12: Initial alert received from monitoring rule; escalated to Security. Noticed common referrer header across exchanges.
Security (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-12: Marking as P1 Sev1 due to clustered rotation pattern; advised immediate rotation of refresh tokens and revocation of active sessions for affected service accounts.

SRE (Diego Ramos) - 2026-03-12: Revoked active sessions and rotated client credentials for svc-data-pipeline and svc-recruiting-parser. Applied temporary rate-limit on token-exchange endpoint for internal-client. Collecting full auth logs for 10:00-12:00 UTC.

Recruiting team (Liam O'Connor) - 2026-03-13: Vendor form flagged; vendor confirmed a legacy redirector parameter remains in their flow and is used by third-party analytics. Vendor committed to patching open-redirect by 2026-03-18.
Security (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-14: Found no lateral privilege escalation from rotated tokens; continuing audit of other service accounts for similar patterns.
SRE (Diego Ramos) - 2026-03-14: Added threshold alert to trigger at >10 refresh exchanges per account per hour and blocked referrer host at the WAF-level as temporary mitigation.
Support (Avery Chen) - 2026-03-14: Notifying internal app owners and scheduling a post-incident review.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Malicious actor obtained valid refresh tokens from a compromised recruiting vendor redirector that allowed token replay via open-redirect analytics parameter.
Hypothesis 2: Internal automation (vendor onboarding job) misconfigured to retry refresh on 5xx and leaked tokens to third-party tracing endpoint; less likely given IP diversity.

Logs indicate same referrer header for all exchange requests; referrer resolves to third-party vendor form used by recruiting. HTTP Referer header may have been included by the service that performed the token exchange (legacy UI).
No suspicious console or code commits found in past 48 hours that would cause automated refresh storms. Checked CI logs and onboarding scripts; no direct matches.
Geo analysis: IPs span three distinct cloud provider regions; likely opportunistic reuse of tokens or distributed proxying rather than single compromised internal host.

Telemetry: token-use patterns show immediate API calls using new access tokens against internal indexer for 15-35 seconds after issuance — typical indicator of automated ingestion vs. interactive human use.
resolution: Immediate actions taken (2026-03-12): rotated refresh tokens and client secrets for the three affected service accounts; revoked all active sessions; applied temporary WAF block for the vendor referrer; added per-account refresh-exchange rate-limiting for internal-client.

Medium-term mitigations (by 2026-03-18): vendor patch to remove open-redirect param; updated onboarding integration docs to disallow refresh-token reuse to external hosts; added MFA requirement and conditional access for service onboarding UI.

Follow-ups: security to run a 7-day audit of all service-account refresh rates; platform to add anomaly-based detection for clustered rotations and immediate automated lockout; post-incident review scheduled 2026-03-20 in #sec-postmortems.
Current status: containment achieved, monitoring in elevated state, incident remains In Progress until full 7-day audit completes and vendor fix verified.
